title: Abba son of Rav Minyamin (Menyumi or Binyamin) bar Chiyya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was the student of Rav Huna bar Chiyya (Chullin 80a: he asked Rav Huna bar Chiyya), and it is very likely to say that he was the reciter in the academy of Rav Huna, as we always find: "Abba the son of Rav Menyumi bar Chiyya taught" (Yevamot 102b; Niddah 13b), or "Abba the son of Rav Binyamin bar Chiyya taught" (at the end of Rosh Hashanah; Sotah 38b). In Dikdukei Soferim the reading is "the son of Rav Minyamin bar Chiyya." The statement in Sotah is cited in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot ch. 5 halakhah 4 and Gittin ch. 5 halakhah 9 in the name of Abaye bar Rabbi Binyamin.

Some wish to say that he is Abba bar Menyumi, who is Abba bar Marta. This is not correct, because this Abba is always mentioned as the son "of Rav," whereas the latter has no title Rav. Nor is he Abba bar Binyamin, since he was in Babylonia while the latter was in Eretz Israel, as explained in his entry.

notes.text: Minyamin, Menyumi and Binyamin are preserved as variants. A tanna in an amoraic academy can mean a reciter of traditions.

The notice abbreviates the teacher’s name as ר״ה. The corresponding passage in the vocalized William Davidson text of Chullin 80a names Rav Huna bar Chiyya. Abba’s further role as a reciter in his academy is Hyman’s suggestion.
